compiled_by: Claude, from a PubMed and Semantic Scholar search of skull base foramen morphometry
USAGE: ADVISORY FLAGGING ONLY. These values must never reject a measurement, never
constrain the manual arm, and never alter a recorded value. They exist to draw
a human's attention to a value that looks unusual, nothing more.
The reason is that this study exists to characterise SPG-region anatomy for
device design. If published windows were used to reject outliers, the study
would partly be measuring its own priors and could mask exactly the anatomical
variation the NINS device has to accommodate. A subject outside these bands is
a subject to LOOK AT, not a subject to exclude.
DEFINITIONAL MISMATCH IS REAL AND LARGE. Most of these come from surgical and
endoscopic landmark studies whose landmark definitions differ from this
protocol's Appendix A. The clearest demonstration is inside this very file:
SPF to hard palate is reported at 15.58 mm while SPF to nasal floor is reported
at 26.6 mm. Those are different landmarks measured differently, not a
contradiction, and treating either as a bound on the other would be wrong.
Every entry therefore carries a definition_note and a confidence field.

2026-08-06 addition: no study found in this search reports inter or intra-observer reliability for any of these measurements. That is a genuine gap in the literature and one this study is positioned to fill, since it measures 3 times per subject per side by a single measurer.

isaacs2007.citation: Isaacs S, Goyal P. Endoscopic anatomy of the pterygopalatine fossa. Am J Rhinol. 2007

gupta2019.citation: Gupta T, et al. Landmarks for Accurate Sphenopalatine Ganglion Block Via the Transnasal and Infrazygomatic Approaches: A Cadaveric Study. Neurosurgery. 2019
gupta2019.design: 30 mid-sagittal cadaveric head and neck sections, digital vernier caliper

spielman2019.citation: Spielman D, et al. Locating and Preserving the Sphenopalatine Ganglion in Endoscopic Endonasal Pterygopalatine Fossa Surgery: An Anatomical Study. Am J Rhinol Allergy. 2019

hwang2011.citation: Hwang S, et al. Three-Dimensional Computed Tomography Analysis to Help Define an Endoscopic Endonasal Approach of the Pterygopalatine Fossa. Am J Rhinol Allergy. 2011

sir2019.citation: Sir E, et al. Morphological Description and Clinical Implication of Sphenopalatine Foramen for Accurate Transnasal Sphenopalatine Ganglion Block: An Anatomical Study. Medeniyet Med J. 2019

mansour2017.citation: Landmarks for rapid localization of the sphenopalatine foramen: A radiographic morphometric analysis. Allergy Rhinol (Providence). 2017

sahin2016.citation: The sphenoid sinus, foramen rotundum and vidian canal: a radiological study of anatomical relationships. Braz J Otorhinolaryngol. 2016

munteanu2026.citation: Munteanu IM, et al. Cone-Beam CT Morphometry of the Foramen Rotundum and Adjacent Skull-Base Landmarks. J Craniofac Surg. 2026

vidiancbct2019.citation: Morphometric analysis of vidian canal and its relations with surrounding anatomic structures by using cone-beam computed tomography. Folia Morphol (Warsz). 2019

stajcic2010.citation: Stojcev Stajcic L, et al. Anatomical study of the pterygopalatine fossa pertinent to the maxillary nerve block at the foramen rotundum. Int J Oral Maxillofac Surg. 2010
stajcic2010.design: 85 dried human skulls, 159 intact pterygopalatine fossae

chen2010.citation: Chen CC, et al. Comparative research of the thin transverse sectional anatomy and the multislice spiral CT on Pterygopalatine Fossa. Turk Neurosurg. 2010
chen2010.design: cadaveric 0.1 mm serial sectioning vs 0.6 mm MSCT

machado2022.citation: Machado A, et al. Greater Palatine Canal: Computed Tomography-Based Anatomic Analysis. Ear Nose Throat J. 2022

moideen2025.citation: Moideen SP, Joseph T, Thomas I, Joseph NA, Pulimoottil DT. A Radiographic Morphometric Analysis for the Preoperative Localization of the Sphenopalatine Artery. Indian J Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 2025;77(3):1424-1428
moideen2025.design: retrospective paranasal sinus CT, 1 mm reconstructions, manual measurement, 100 sides

priors.quantity: 3D distance from the sphenopalatine foramen to the sphenopalatine ganglion
priors.definition_note: Three independent cadaveric studies converge. Gupta reports 4 mm posterior and 4.7 mm lateral, resultant 6.3 mm. Isaacs reports 4 mm medially and 6 mm laterally. Spielman reports 4.5 +/- 1.1 mm lateral and 1 +/- 1.4 mm inferior. The SPG is consistently LATERAL and slightly posterior or inferior to the SPF.
priors.used_for: sanity check on the computed SPG centroid against the SPF_inf landmark. A centroid far outside this band means the three input lines were misplaced, not that the anatomy is unusual.

priors.quantity: sphenopalatine foramen aperture diameter
priors.definition_note: Hwang gives a single mean diameter of 5.3 +/- 1.3 mm on 3D CT. Sir gives width 3.79 +/- 0.35 mm and length 6.44 +/- 0.94 mm on cadaver and dry skull, so the foramen is an ellipse rather than a circle. The study's axial and coronal diameters are therefore expected to DIFFER from each other, and should bracket rather than match the single-value estimate.

priors.quantity: anterior nasal spine to sphenopalatine foramen
priors.definition_note: Sir 52.90 +/- 2.98 mm, Gupta 55 mm at a mean elevation of 22 to 26 degrees from the hard palate. Both are cadaver or dry skull. A separate radiographic study measuring from the NASAL SILL rather than ANS gives 64.4 +/- 6 mm, which is a different landmark and is deliberately not pooled here.

priors.quantity: sphenopalatine foramen to foramen rotundum
priors.definition_note: Single cadaveric source, no dispersion reported. Treat as an order-of-magnitude anchor only.
maps_to_measurement_keys: INF FORAMEN ROTUNDUM to SPF - CORONAL, Summed (mm)

priors.quantity: sphenopalatine foramen to nasal floor, vertical
priors.definition_note: Moideen 2025 gives 23.6 plus or minus 4.6 mm on 100 sides, Mansour 2017 gives 26.6 plus or minus 2.6 mm. These overlap within their SDs and are treated as converging. Both are vertical SPF to NASAL FLOOR on coronal cuts. Still distinct from spf_to_hard_palate at 15.58 mm, which is a different reference surface and must not be pooled with these.

priors.quantity: sphenopalatine foramen to hard palate
priors.definition_note: See the conflict noted in spf_to_nasal_floor. Dry skull and cadaver measurement.

priors.quantity: inferior bony border of SPF to the cranial entrance of the greater palatine canal
priors.definition_note: CT-based, 200 sides, no significant side difference. Relevant because the study's GP canal sagittal line is one of the three SPG centroid inputs.

priors.quantity: vidian canal to the posteroinferior margin of the SPF
priors.definition_note: The vidian canal lies above the inferior SPF margin in 92 percent of sides and lateral to the posterior SPF margin in 98 percent. Useful as a topological expectation for the pterygoid seed, which is anchored on the operator's vidian line.

priors.quantity: foramen rotundum to skull base midline
priors.definition_note: Right 19.00 +/- 2.07 mm, left 19.34 +/- 2.17 mm, n = 100 CT. Mean bilateral FR separation 38.48 +/- 3.87 mm. A statistically significant but sub-millimetre side difference.
priors.used_for: independent sanity check on the midline estimate and on the FR_inf landmark, and a bound for the sphenoid seed box

priors.quantity: foramen rotundum to vidian canal, direct
priors.definition_note: Munteanu 8.70 +/- 1.90 mm direct. Hwang decomposes it as 5.8 +/- 1.9 mm vertical and 8.5 +/- 1.9 mm horizontal on the sphenoid surface plane, which is consistent with the direct distance.
priors.used_for: spacing sanity between the pterygoid and sphenoid seeds

priors.quantity: vidian canal length
priors.used_for: sanity bound on PTERYGOID_EXTEND_MM, which extends the vidian seed posteriorly

priors.quantity: vidian canal diameter
priors.definition_note: Constrains PTERYGOID_SEED_R_MM: a seed radius much larger than the canal itself will recruit neighbouring bone indiscriminately.

priors.quantity: foramen rotundum diameter
priors.definition_note: Munteanu separately reports an FR height of 5.11 +/- 1.68 mm, which is the canal's cross-sectional height rather than its bore, so the two are not directly comparable.

priors.quantity: pterygopalatine fossa width
priors.definition_note: 85 dried skulls. The authors explicitly describe the dimensions as INCONSISTENT: volume 0.1 to 1 cm3, width 1 to 9 mm, depth 6 to 22 mm. This ninefold width range is the single strongest argument in this file against using literature values as rejection criteria.
priors.used_for: palatine and pterygoid seed box scale

priors.quantity: pterygopalatine fossa depth
priors.definition_note: See pterygopalatine_fossa_width.

priors.quantity: sphenopalatine ganglion itself, cross-section at its largest layer
priors.definition_note: 3.91 x 1.92 mm from 0.1 mm cadaveric serial sectioning, n = 2 heads. Very small n, but it is the only direct measurement of the ganglion found and is directly relevant to NINS device sizing: the target is a roughly 4 x 2 mm structure.
priors.used_for: device design criteria context, not segmentation

priors.quantity: sphenopalatine foramen to basal lamella of the middle turbinate, anteroposterior
priors.definition_note: CONFLICT, and it matters. Moideen 2025 reports 7.5 plus or minus 2.0 mm on 100 sides; Mansour 2017 reports 11.8 plus or minus 1.9 mm. The means differ by 4.3 mm and the SDs barely overlap, so this is unlikely to be sampling noise. The basal lamella is a broad plate rather than a point, so the two studies are probably measuring to different parts of it. Consequence for this study: the basal lamella was proposed as the posterior anchor for both middle turbinate curves, and it cannot serve as a reproducible anchor until WHICH PART of the lamella is specified. Resolve before the reference pass.
priors.used_for: proposed anchor for MT_medial_ax, MT_medial_cor and MT_inferior_cor

priors.quantity: sphenopalatine foramen to maxillary line, anteroposterior
priors.definition_note: Moideen 2025 36.3 plus or minus 2.3 mm, Mansour 2017 36.7 plus or minus 5.5 mm. Close agreement on the mean and Moideen more than halves the SD. One of the tightest SPF relationships published.

priors.quantity: sphenopalatine foramen to anterior head of middle turbinate, anteroposterior
priors.definition_note: Moideen 2025 34.8 plus or minus 3.1 mm, Mansour 2017 33.8 plus or minus 6.7 mm. Converging, with Moideen again considerably tighter.

priors.quantity: sphenopalatine foramen to choanal arch, anteroposterior
priors.definition_note: Moideen 2025 9.0 plus or minus 1.8 mm, Mansour 2017 9.2 plus or minus 1.4 mm. Two independent CT studies agreeing to 0.2 mm. The most reliably reproduced SPF relationship found, which supports the choanal arch as a posterior anchor.
